name: Crac des Chevaliers and Qal’at Salah El-Din
description: Two hilltop castles in western Syria show how Crusader and Muslim military builders borrowed from one another. Crac des Chevaliers, near Homs, was raised by the Knights Hospitaller from 1142 and later strengthened by the Mamluks. Its concentric walls make it one of the best-preserved Crusader castles. Qal'at Salah El-Din, partly ruined, layers Byzantine, Frankish and Ayyubid stonework.
